subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public anti-herd scheduling contract for heartbeat and cron every schedules, and should that contract be prime cadence, deterministic phase/stagger, fixed-time phase, or a narrower extension of existing cron stagger behavior?
rationale: Current source already implements stable heartbeat phasing and cron-expression staggering, but the remaining request would define public config, CLI, protocol/persisted schedule semantics, defaults, and upgrade behavior that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design one scheduler contract
options.body: Add a single documented anti-herd model for heartbeat and cron every schedules with compatibility-preserving defaults, persisted schema behavior, CLI/status docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Limit to cron every stagger
options.body: Extend the existing cron stagger model to every schedules while treating heartbeat's shipped stable phase as sufficient for now.

options.title: Decline new timing knobs
options.body: Keep fixed-interval semantics plus existing heartbeat phase and cron-expression staggering, and close this only after maintainers state prime/phase controls are out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design one scheduler contract
recommendation.body: Add a single documented anti-herd model for heartbeat and cron every schedules with compatibility-preserving defaults, persisted schema behavior, CLI/status docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent evidence across cron stagger fixes, cron schedule behavior, and scheduler-adjacent review history.
